result.title: Nous: Learning and Certifying Memory Decisions Before Source Calibration
result.comment: 19 pages, 3 figures; code and reproducibility package available at https://github.com/Pranavsingh431/nous-state/tree/main/research/decision-certification
result.summary: Belief-based agent memory needs reliable decisions about current state, yet its evidence may be noisy, copied, or stale. Must a memory calibrate its sources before it can improve its decisions? We separate learning, calibration, and revision certification. On one four-model hidden Markov family, learning an unknown Bayes decision requires Theta(l^-2) records and certifying its improvement over an informative incumbent takes O(l^-2) fresh records from the same observation law, while fixed-precision source estimation requires Theta(l^-4) as persistence l vanishes. Thus learning and certifying useful decisions can require quadratically fewer records than source calibration. A broader model class retains the decision rate and source lower bound. Under an unknown identity-plus-background report channel, we characterize the sharp identified interval for policy improvement and derive a finite-sample certificate using observable witness regions, without pure-class anchors. A robustness extension tolerates bounded history-dependent misspecification and conditional copying; split-trained witnesses apply to arbitrary history spaces with explicit power conditions. We integrate policy-bound receipts with Nous Dimensions and test 45,000 held-out mutable-state histories and 9,000 episodes in three external MiniGrid memory environments with an introduced noisy-report interface. The new certificate accepts 9/9 improvements over a constant incumbent and 4/9 over last-write-wins, versus none for the earlier certificate in MiniGrid. Strong established inference baselines remain competitive or better. The result is a statistical account of when memory decisions can be learned and justified without recovering source reliability, not a universally superior memory algorithm.

AI.brief_summary: Nous 研究带噪声、复制或过期证据的信念式 agent 记忆：将学习、源校准与修正认证分离，在隐马尔可夫模型族上给出决策学习与认证所需样本量随持久度 l 的 Theta 阶刻画，并在 MiniGrid 记忆中评测可观测见证区域构造的有限样本证书。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于「无需恢复源可靠性即可学习并认证记忆决策」的样本复杂度与可观测见证区域证书，可能为 LVR 中在噪声视觉证据下判断 latent 状态是否可用、以及停止/修订决策的可靠性评价提供概念工具，但需核查其观测模型与 VLM 内部状态的可迁移性。
